answer.line: Same base, so count the 5s: one 5 times six 5s is seven 5s, 5^7 = 78125.

steps: Count the factors. 5^1 is one 5; 5^6 is six 5s multiplied together.
Put them side by side: seven 5s in a row, so 5^1 x 5^6 = 5^7. Add the exponents; the base stays 5.
Evaluate: 5^6 = 15625, and one more 5 gives 5 x 15625 = 78125.

choices.note: A product of 5s is never 0, so no rule lands here. A product is 0 only when one factor is 0, and every factor here is 5.
1 x 6 = 6 multiplies the exponents and lands on 5^6. Multiplying powers of one base adds the exponents: 1 + 6 = 7.
5 + 15625 = 15630 adds the two powers. The stem multiplies them: 5 x 15625 = 78125.
Adding the exponents is right, but the base must stay 5. Multiplying 5 x 5 into 25 gives 25^7, far too big.

lockIt: Same base multiplied: add the exponents and keep the base.

playWith.label: Exponent Laws: pick multiply, set the base and both powers, and watch the exponents add

visual.caption: Count the circles. One 5 and six 5s make seven 5s, so the exponents add.
